narrative.summary: States parties to the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons have discussed lethal autonomous weapons systems in a Group of Governmental Experts since 2017. In 2019 the High Contracting Parties endorsed eleven Guiding Principles, including that international humanitarian law applies fully to these systems and that human responsibility for decisions on the use of weapons must be retained. The Group's 2023 report added consensus conclusions on compliance with international humanitarian law across the life cycle of such systems. Under its 2024–2026 mandate the Group has worked on a set of elements of a possible instrument, to be reported to the Seventh Review Conference in November 2026.

instruments.summary: Eleven guiding principles on lethal autonomous weapons systems. They state that international humanitarian law applies fully to all weapons systems; human responsibility for decisions on the use of weapons must be retained across the system life cycle; human-machine interaction must ensure compliance with international law; accountability must run through a responsible chain of human command and control; new weapons must be legally reviewed; cyber security, proliferation and terrorist-acquisition risks and risk mitigation must be considered; the technologies should not be anthropomorphized; peaceful uses should not be hampered; and the CCW is an appropriate framework.
instruments.current_status: Guiding Principles affirmed by the Group of Governmental Experts, annexed (Annex III) to the final report of the 2019 Meeting of the High Contracting Parties (Geneva, 13-15 November 2019), issued as CCW/MSP/2019/9 on 13 December 2019.

Endorsement wording: the GGE 2019 report recommended HCPs endorse the principles; GGE 2023 report para 17 refers to 'the Guiding Principles endorsed in 2019'. instruments.summary: Report of the CCW expert group of states. Its conclusions acknowledge the 2019 Guiding Principles and state that international humanitarian law continues to apply fully to the potential development and use of lethal autonomous weapons systems; systems that cannot be used in compliance with it must not be used; states must ensure compliance throughout the life cycle, limiting types of targets, duration, geographical scope and scale of operations where necessary and providing training and instructions to operators; and states must determine whether employment of new weapons would be prohibited by international law. Voluntary exchange of best practices is encouraged.
instruments.current_status: Adopted by the Group of Governmental Experts on 19 May 2023 (advance version dated 24 May 2023). It recommends that the 2023 Meeting of the High Contracting Parties decide by consensus on the modalities of the Group's future work.
